name: OM-89
question: Does oral OM-89 reduce recurrent urinary tract infections in women compared with placebo over 12 months?

design.population: 454 adult women with recurrent uncomplicated UTI and acute UTI with at least 10³ bacteria/mL at enrollment were randomized; 453 received treatment.
design.locator: Publisher indexed article, Methods and Results; PubMed abstract, Methods

verdictNote: Fewer post-baseline UTIs and fewer women with recurrence over 12 months.
takeaway: In women with recurrent UTI, oral Escherichia coli extract OM-89 reduced the mean post-baseline UTI rate over 12 months versus matching placebo (0.84 versus 1.28; p < 0.003).

reports.label: 12-month primary report
reports.citation: Bauer HW, Alloussi S, Egger G, Blümlein HM, Cozma G, Schulman CC. "A long-term, multicenter, double-blind study of an Escherichia coli extract (OM-89) in female patients with recurrent urinary tract infections." *Eur Urol.* 2005;47(4):542-548. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2004.12.009

results.measure: Difference in mean post-baseline UTI rate over 12 months
results.note: Mean difference calculated from the reported group means; the report describes a 34% reduction.

results.endpoint: Women with at least one post-baseline UTI
results.measure: Proportion with post-baseline UTI over 12 months; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Risk difference calculated from the reported rounded percentages.

results.measure: Observed post-baseline UTI episodes among treated women over 12 months
results.note: The abstract does not give a separate test for the prespecified distribution-of-UTIs criterion.

delivery.label: Oral treatment schedule

values.exp: One OM-89 capsule daily for 90 days, then the first 10 days of months 7, 8, and 9
values.ctl: One matching placebo capsule on the same schedule

delivery.note: No study capsule was given during months 4 through 6.
